issue.body:
I wanted to try curl master before the release 7.65.1 to verify the fix  #3904. Although core dump was not seen, I see sendto going in tight loop after some few transfers and application consumes 100% CPU, I also don't see the case of GOAWAY being sent by server here.

### I did this
Use curl-master before 7.65.1 for check for HTTP/2 traffic run

### I expected the following
Transfers without trap and issues

### curl/libcurl version
curl master as of 3rd Jun before 7.65.1 release

### operating system
Fedora 28

Following is the pstack output when it goes to 100% CPU:
Thread 1 (Thread 0x7fb0ef47e780 (LWP 26)):
#0  0x00007fb0d29af09e in send () from /usr/lib64/libpthread.so.0
#1  0x00007fb0edf1a970 in Curl_send_plain () from /usr/lib/libBase.so
#2  0x00007fb0edf1a40d in Curl_write () from /usr/lib/libBase.so
#3  0x00007fb0edf16268 in Curl_add_buffer_send () from  /usr/lib/libBase.so
#4  0x00007fb0edf178b9 in Curl_http () from /usr/lib/libBase.so
#5  0x00007fb0edefc706 in multi_runsingle () from  /usr/lib/libBase.so
#6  0x00007fb0edefd6ae in multi_socket () from  /usr/lib/libBase.so
#7  0x00007fb0edefd805 in curl_multi_socket_action () from /usr/lib/libBase.so
#8  0x00007fb0ede887dd in HttpClient::TimerTriggered (this=0x4005200) at httpClient.cc:287

strace output:
sendto(-1, "POST /worker/help1"..., 155, MSG_NOSIGNAL, NULL, 0) = -1
EBADF (Bad file descriptor)
sendto(-1, "POST  /worker/help1"..., 155, MSG_NOSIGNAL, NULL, 0) = -1
EBADF (Bad file descriptor)
sendto(-1, "POST  /worker/help1"..., 155, MSG_NOSIGNAL, NULL, 0) = -1
EBADF (Bad file descriptor)
sendto(-1, "P
...

Although the issue is easily reproduced, I'm yet to provide a program which simulates this.

body:
I don't know why but I can't get this code to run, presumably since something is wrong with my build. The make command reports no problems but when I try to run it:

     $ perl -Mblib t/curlbug.t  >/dev/null
     perl: symbol lookup error: /home/daniel/src/perl-AnyEvent-YACurl/AnyEvent-YACurl/blib/arch/auto/AnyEvent/YACurl/YACurl.so: undefined symbol: curl_global_init

I have a static libcurl build in my source code tree that I point out with `CURL_CONFIG` and from my inspection the generated `Makefile` looks like gets some of the flags right at least... ldd shows no dynamic libcurl being used:

    $ ldd blib/arch/auto/AnyEvent/YACurl/YACurl.so 
        linux-vdso.so.1 (0x00007fffd01d4000)
        libc.so.6 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6 (0x00007ff96e370000)
        /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 (0x00007ff96e58a000)

I followed this and it worked for me:
1. CURL_CONFIG=<specific_path>/bin/curl-config perl Makefile.PL --static-libs
2. Modified Makefile
   a. INC = -I. -I/usr/libcurlnghttp2/include -I/usr/include/nghttp2
   b. OBJECT = $(O_FILES) /usr/libcurlnghttp2/lib64/libcurl.a
   c. EXTRALIBS = /usr/lib64/libnghttp2.so.14.16.2 -lssl -lcrypto -lssl -lcrypto -lz
       LDLOADLIBS = /usr/lib64/libnghttp2.so.14.16.2 -lssl -lcrypto -lssl -lcrypto -lz
   d. PASTHRU_INC='-I. -I/usr/libcurlnghttp2/include -I/usr/include/nghttp2 $(PASTHRU_INC)'
3. make
4. perl -Mblib t/curlbug.t  >/dev/null

Basically, I saw that Makefile is not referring to correct paths.

I had to also install perl-devel, perl-AnyEvent

BTW, an initial thing to test is to just remove the `DEBUGASSERT(NULL);` line and see what happens.

It is placed there simply because that's a situation that shouldn't occur (it wants to remove the transfer as a user of the socket but for some reason it doesn't find the transfer there), but it is also quite likely a situation that isn't lethal - which is why it is only an assert (ie not present in a non-debug build).

Yeah I tried it :) same time, it results in trap at some other place. I can update with the bt here.
update(just for reference incase) : If the that assert is removed, other place where it traps is:
`multi.c:2514: multi_socket: Assertion `data-\u003emagic == 0xc0dedbadU' failed.`
I don't think that'll help me.

Looks like the .so file produced by the Makefile wasn't actually linked to libcurl.a. That could be because curl-config doesn't output the .a file in your case? Not sure. Mine looks like this:

    $ /home/tom/code/curl-lib/bin/curl-config --static-libs --cflags
    /home/tom/code/curl-lib/lib/libcurl.a -L/home/tom/code/nghttp2-lib/lib -lnghttp2 -lssl -lcrypto -lssl -lcrypto
    -DCURL_STATICLIB -I/home/tom/code/curl-lib/include

Anyway, let's avoid debugging the makefile and just bypass it. The correct command for compiling the .so file (after make has run to compile the other stuff) would look like

    cc -shared -L/usr/local/lib YACurl.o /home/tom/code/curl-lib/lib/libcurl.a  -o blib/arch/auto/AnyEvent/YACurl/YACurl.so     -L/home/tom/code/nghttp2-lib/lib -lnghttp2 -lssl -lcrypto

After this, you should have a .so file linked to at least an ssl library:

    $ ldd blib/arch/auto/AnyEvent/YACurl/YACurl.so
        linux-vdso.so.1 (0x00007fffe06c7000)
        libssl.so.1.1 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libssl.so.1.1 (0x00007f40b4740000)
        libcrypto.so.1.1 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcrypto.so.1.1 (0x00007f40b4270000)
        libc.so.6 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6 (0x00007f40b3e70000)
        libpthread.so.0 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libpthread.so.0 (0x00007f40b3c50000)
        libdl.so.2 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libdl.so.2 (0x00007f40b3a40000)
        /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 (0x00007f40b4e00000)

and then the bug should be reproducible:

    $ perl -Mblib t/curlbug.t >/dev/null
    perl: multi.c:2359: singlesocket: Assertion `((void *)0)' failed.
    Aborted (core dumped)

(As @kunalekawde noted, this needs the AnyEvent perl library to be installed, in RHEL you can find it as perl-AnyEvent, in Debian/Ubuntu as libanyevent-perl)

> 
> 
> BTW, an initial thing to test is to just remove the `DEBUGASSERT(NULL);` line and see what happens.
> 
> It is placed there simply because that's a situation that shouldn't occur (it wants to remove the transfer as a user of the socket but for some reason it doesn't find the transfer there), but it is also quite likely a situation that isn't lethal - which is why it is only an assert (ie not present in a non-debug build).

@bagder , I'm not exactly sure on interpretation but I had posted gdb frame details in #3991 https://github.com/curl/curl/issues/3991#issuecomment-501143663, where it appeared that although the deletion was unsuccessful, the same key was present (based on first few bytes seen in gdb) at some other location. Based on which I tried a temp hack. Do you think that data could be still present in some other bucket , pls ignore if its sounds silly ;)
Thanks @TvdW, I made it build and can reproduce with it.

body: @bagder , I had attempted similar fix at https://github.com/curl/curl/issues/3991#issuecomment-501253336 but it failed when I ran multiple times with some time period of ~2-3min between executions resulting in trap. I tried this fix also and it resulted in trap. Although the test program shared by @TvdW runs fine using this patch most likely because the connections are torn down after each run.  Do you think I should open another issue for same and also close #3991 ?

I don't understand what "similar fix" you did because clearly the hash removal was plain wrong before this (#4024) so the fix is correct no matter what. It might of course not be the final fix.

> I tried this fix also and it resulted in trap. 

That would imply there are more issues. @TvdW told me (on twitter) he still see problems as well.

>  Do you think I should open another issue for same and also close #3991 ?

Unfortunately it doesn't matter very much what you do with them as long as nobody else can reproduce the problems. Or perhaps if you can instrument the code good enough around the particular crash point to provide information enough to enlighten someone what the issue might be, but that's also hard work.
